teksty.Do rozpoznawania nut ze skanu potrzebny:
Recognising scores from a scan needs the free program Audiveris (installed separately, about 130 MB, with Java built in).

Windows / macOS / Ubuntu: download the installer from the Assets section of the latest release (.msi, .dmg or .deb file).
Linux (Flatpak): flatpak install flathub org.audiveris.audiveris

After installation Liber Canticorum finds it by itself; if not – Settings → Path to Audiveris.

teksty.<h3>Podziel się melodią lub aranżacją</h:
Share a melody or arrangement

A melody you entered, or your setting for schola, choir or organ, can help other communities. Share it on MuseScore.com (free account) with an open licence:

  • CC0 / public domain – anyone may use it without restriction,
  • CC BY or CC BY-SA – anyone may use and adapt it, crediting you as the author (with BY-SA – under the same licence).

How: 1. “Export MusicXML…” (or save as .mscz in MuseScore), 2. “Upload” on MuseScore.com, 3. give the source of the melody and text in the description, 4. choose CC0 or CC BY / CC BY-SA as the licence, 5. add tags, e.g. liturgy, schola, psalm, Advent.

Note: share only what you have the right to – your own settings and public-domain melodies. The words and the original tune may belong to other authors: check their rights (see Help → “© Song copyright”). Thank you – this is how a good common songbook for everyone grows!

  1. Click “Search MuseScore” – a browser opens with results for the title.

teksty.<h2>Prawa autorskie do pieśni – krótko i:
Song copyright – briefly and kindly

The program is free, but the lyrics, melodies and scores you put into it have their authors. Rights to songs can be complex – one song is often several works at once:

  • the text (the author of the words and, for translated songs, the translator),
  • the melody (the composer),
  • the setting – harmonisation, arrangement for choir or organ, accompaniment,
  • the edition – editing of the text, music engraving, preparation of the songbook.

In Poland and the EU economic copyright generally expires 70 years after the author's death (for a song written jointly by a lyricist and a composer – after the death of the one who died later). An old song may therefore be free, while its modern edition, new translation or harmonisation is not. “Folk” and “traditional” songs also often have newer, protected versions of the text.

Polish law allows the use of works during religious ceremonies if no direct or indirect financial gain is involved (art. 31(1) of the Polish Copyright Act); the rules in your country may differ. Concerts, recordings shared online, broadcasts, copying and distributing songbooks or scores are a different matter – here the permission of the authors or publishers is usually needed (e.g. through a collecting society or directly). Liturgical texts (readings, psalms, prayers) belong to the publishers of the liturgical books.

Please: respect the work of authors and publishers – give the source (in the song notes), do not publish other people's scores and recordings online without permission, and treat the songbooks made by the program (PDF, HTML) as an aid for your own community. This is not legal advice – if in doubt, ask the publisher, a collecting society or a lawyer.

Good sources of texts and scores

It is best to use reliable, carefully edited editions – they have correct texts approved for the liturgy and documented sources:

  • the official hymnals and songbooks of your bishops' conference or diocese,
  • Śpiewnik kościelny of Fr. Jan Siedlecki – spiewniksiedleckiego.pl (Polish texts with melody recordings),
  • the Missal, the Lectionary, the Graduale – liturgical texts (chants between the readings, antiphons),
  • public-domain scores: CPDL (choral), IMSLP; on MuseScore check the licence of the arrangement.

Chants intended for the liturgy should be approved by the bishops' conference or the diocesan authority.

Share your own work

Have you entered a melody or prepared your own setting (for schola, choir, organ)? Share it on MuseScore.com with an open licence – CC0 (public domain) or CC BY / CC BY-SA – so that other communities can use it. In the melody editor: “🌍 Share on MuseScore.com…”. Share only what you have the right to: your own settings and public-domain melodies; give the source of the tune and the words in the description.

Church documents on music

  • Second Vatican Council, constitution Sacrosanctum Concilium (1963), ch. VI “Sacred Music” – the foundation,
  • Instruction Musicam sacram (1967),
  • Instruction of the Polish Bishops' Conference on liturgical music after the Second Vatican Council (1979) – text (Polish),
  • St John Paul II, Letter to Artists (1999),
  • St John Paul II, Chirograph for the centenary of the motu proprio “Tra le sollecitudini” on sacred music (22.11.2003) – on vatican.va,
  • Benedict XVI, exhortation Sacramentum caritatis (2007), no. 42 – on liturgical singing,
  • Instruction of the Polish Bishops' Conference on church music (14.10.2017) – in force in Poland – text (Polish),
  • Francis, apostolic letter Desiderio desideravi on liturgical formation (2022).

Polish Copyright and Related Rights Act (consolidated text, Journal of Laws 2025 item 24): PDF.

teksty.Najlepiej wesprzesz nas, śpiewając razem: You support us best by singing with us: at Mass on the first Sunday of the month at noon in the church in Laski (ul. 3 Maja 40/42); we rehearse on Tuesdays at 19:00 in the parish house. Invite your friends and family too! Live far away – even on another continent? Pray with us on the first Sunday of the month and send us your intention (contact on the schola's website) – we will commend it to God at Mass.
teksty.Kochamy muzykę – zwłaszcza chóralną i tę: We love music – especially choral music and the music that accompanies the liturgy – and we cannot help singing :-). With our singing we serve the community of the parish of Our Lady Queen of Mexico in Laski (Poland); the rays in our logo stand for wonder at God's unfathomable work. We are responsible for the Mass for abundant grace for families – past, present and future, in all their needs (this is not the prosperity gospel :-) ). We pray for your family too ;-).

teksty.Schola adHoc działa przy parafii M.B. Kr: Schola adHoc sings at the parish of Our Lady, Queen of Mexico, in Laski (Poland). Every first Sunday of the month we pray in song during Mass for an abundance of grace for families. Send us your intention and pray with us in song :-). ATTENTION! The Holy Spirit works mightily through the intercession of our Queen.

Each row is one song. Select rows (Ctrl or Shift for several) and use the buttons below the list.
➕ New – adds the song to the database. 🔗 Merge – this song is already in the database: the lyrics are added to it as a version, nothing is overwritten. ⛔ Skip – do not import. ✂ Split – when one file contains several songs.
